text:
You will see the wonder of the road,

road of dreamed Compostela

—oh lilac and tawny mountain!— pilgrim,

on a plain, among candle poplars.

Autumn with two rivers has gilded

the enclosure of the giant sentinel

of stone and light, towered prodigy

that takes shape in the spotless blue.

You will see on the plain a pack

of keen greyhounds and a hunting lord,

riding toward a distant range,

vain phantom of an old race.

You must enter when in the cold afternoon

a balcony shines in the deserted square.




1925

translation.title: You Will See the Wonder of the Road
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the Compostela road, towered sentinel, hunting phantom, and cold shining balcony.
